card.title: Diagnosing HDMI Port issues using Pairs and Patterns technique

source.title: Diagnosing HDMI Port issues using Pairs and Patterns technique

claims.statement: Console HDMI diode readings split into a 'pairs' side and a 'patterns' side; the method applies to all these consoles' HDMI circuits.
claims.evidence: Author's method using a Mechanic T-824 HDMI reader.

claims.statement: Pairs side: four pairs of identical diode readings, each pair separated by a ground reading; the two readings of a pair should match within about ±0.01 V.
Patterns side: readings do not need to match each other but should sit roughly between 0.50 and 0.70 V.
claims.evidence: Example 0.70 and 0.56 both counted as good.

claims.statement: Diode readings roughly in the 0.00–0.30 or 0.90–1.00 zones are usually a sign of a fault, though not always.
claims.evidence: General range guidance in the guide.

claims.statement: On Xbox One X, Series S and Series X, board pin 14 (pin 17 on the reader) shows a diode reading rather than OL; Series X shows OL there until the top board is attached.
claims.evidence: Model-specific exception noted in the guide.

claims.statement: The pairs side runs straight to the encoder/retimer through filters or bidirectional diodes and carries the picture; the patterns side passes a handoff IC (Xbox) or diodes/resistors (PlayStation) and handles negotiation.

procedure: Plug the HDMI reader in and note orientation (pairs may start at the bottom right).
Check the four pairs from one end: identical within ±0.01 V with ground between.
Check the patterns from the other end (starting at line 22): each within about 0.50–0.70 V.
Treat readings near ground or near 0.9–1.0/OL as suspect.

measurements.point: HDMI pairs (each line of a pair)

measurements.context: Rhythm side, values vary within range

card.caveats: Ranges are a technician's rule of thumb; compare with a known-good board of the same revision when possible. Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
